> "Act as a senior Unity developer specializing in Virtual Reality (XR Interaction Toolkit). I am working inside Unity's official VR Template. I need to clean up the default scene and build a functional, cozy coffee shop from scratch. Perform the following tasks step by step:
>  * VR Template Cleanup: Delete all default demo and visual objects from the template scene (test tables, grabbable cubes/balls, tutorial UI boards, sample teleport anchors, and default environment geometry). Keep intact and functional only the core systems required for VR: XR Origin (XR Rig), XR Interaction Manager, EventSystem, hands/controllers, and core locomotion/teleportation managers.
>  * Scene Assembly & Scale: Build the coffee shop using my imported assets. Arrange the architecture (floor, walls, windows), place the main counter on one side, and distribute tables with 2 to 4 chairs around each. Ensure realistic human-scale proportions (1 unit = 1 meter) leaving wide walkways for VR movement, and add a Teleportation Area component to the floor mesh so the player can navigate.
>  * Lighting & Atmosphere: Set up a warm late-afternoon lighting scheme from scratch. Add a Directional Light shining through the storefront windows (set to Mixed or Baked mode with soft shadows), place warm Point Lights or Spot Lights inside the pendant lamps over the tables and counter, add a Reflection Probe in the center of the room for realistic metal and glass reflections, and configure a subtle Global Volume (Post-Processing) with soft Bloom and warm Color Grading.
>  * Collisions (Colliders):
>    * Add static Box Colliders or Mesh Colliders to all non-movable elements (walls, floor, counter, tables, espresso machine).
>    * Add optimized colliders (Box Collider, Capsule Collider, or Mesh Collider strictly set to Convex) to all grabbable objects (chairs, cups, saucers, takeaway cups, trays, pastries, milk pitcher).
>  * Physics & VR Setup (XR Interaction Toolkit):
>    * For chairs and trays: add a Rigidbody (mass: 5 kg for chairs, 0.5 kg for trays; set Angular Drag to 2.5 and Interpolate to Interpolate so they don't jitter or fly away) and an XR Grab Interactable component with Movement Type set to Velocity Tracking so they collide realistically with the floor and tables when moved.
>    * For small props (cups, takeaway cups, food, milk pitcher): add a Rigidbody (mass: 0.2 - 0.5 kg, Interpolate enabled), XR Grab Interactable with Movement Type set to Instantaneous or Velocity Tracking, and create an Attach Transform (empty child GameObject) aligned with the handles of the cups and pitcher for natural hand gripping.
>  * Hierarchy Organization: Organize all scene objects cleanly in the Hierarchy window under empty parent GameObjects named --- VR CORE ---, --- ARCHITECTURE ---, --- STATIC FURNITURE ---, --- VR INTERACTABLES ---, and --- LIGHTING ---."
>

        EditorSceneManager.SaveScene(EditorSceneManager.GetActiveScene());
    }
